faq.question: How much time does it take each week?
faq.answer: About five hours: two live sessions of 75 to 90 minutes and an assignment.

faq.question: What if I miss a live session?
faq.answer: Every session is recorded and posted as a lesson the same day.

faq.question: Do I get a certificate?
faq.answer: Yes. Complete every lesson and the final check to get a certificate with a link anyone can verify.

faq.question: Can my company pay?
faq.answer: Yes. Most learners expense it as professional development. Ask us for an invoice.

faq.question: Is there a refund policy?
faq.answer: If the first week is not for you, tell us before the second live session for a full refund.

modules.name: Week 1 · Frame the decision
modules.description: From a vague problem to real options.

pages.title: Welcome and how the cohort works

fields.objectives: Know the weekly rhythm; Choose the decision you will work on

pages.markdown:
Welcome to the cohort. For three weeks you will work through one product decision of your own, with a small group and two instructors.

**Every week:** a live session on Tuesday, a working session on Thursday, and one assignment you share with your group by Sunday.

**Before Tuesday:** pick the decision you want to work on. A good one is real, yours to make and due within the next quarter.

pages.title: Live session 1: the strategy stack

fields.objectives: Describe strategy as a stack of choices; Write a "will not do" list

pages.markdown:
The recording and slides from the first live session.

Strategy is a stack of choices, each constraining the next: **where we play**, **how we win**, **what we will not do**. Most product teams skip the third, so every request looks equally important.

**Discussion prompt:** what is one thing your team is doing now that a clear "will not do" would stop?

pages.title: Assignment: write your decision brief

fields.objectives: Frame a decision as options; Define how you will judge it

pages.markdown:
In one page, write:

1. The decision, as a question with two or three real options.
2. Who it affects, and how you will know it was right.
3. What you will **not** do, whichever option you choose.

Share it in your group's thread by Sunday. You will give feedback on two others in week 2.

pages.title: Live session 2: evidence, not opinions

fields.objectives: Plan five customer conversations; Set a result that would change your mind

pages.markdown:
How to gather just enough evidence to choose between options — without a six-week research project.

- Five customer conversations beat fifty survey responses for a new question.
- Look for what people **did**, not what they say they would do.
- Decide in advance what result would change your mind.

pages.title: Working session: pressure-test a brief

fields.objectives: Give structured feedback on a brief

pages.markdown:
In pairs, read each other's brief and ask three questions:

1. Which option would you choose today, and why?
2. What evidence would make you choose differently?
3. What is missing from the "will not do" list?

Write down the answers. They are the input to this week's assignment.

pages.title: Assignment: your evidence plan
pages.markdown: Turn the questions from the working session into a plan: who you will talk to, what you will ask, and the result that would change your mind. Keep it to half a page.

modules.name: Week 3 · Make the call
modules.description: Write it, present it, take questions.

pages.title: Live session 3: the narrative
pages.markdown: A decision nobody understands is a decision nobody follows. This session turns your brief into a one-page narrative: the situation, the choice, what it costs, and what happens next.

pages.title: Demo day

fields.objectives: Present a decision and take questions

pages.markdown: Each person presents their decision in five minutes, followed by five minutes of questions from the group and the instructors. Bring the narrative and one slide at most.

pages.title: After the cohort

fields.objectives: Keep using the materials after the cohort

pages.markdown: You keep access to every recording and the community after the cohort ends. Pass the final check to get your certificate, and add it to your profile.

questions.explanation: Without it, every request looks equally important.

questions.prompt: For a new question, which usually tells you more?
questions.explanation: Conversations surface what people did; surveys mostly what they say.

questions.prompt: When should you decide what result would change your mind?
questions.explanation: Deciding afterwards lets you explain away anything.
